    page-layout: full

```{r setup}
# Load required libraries
# NOTE: Install these once manually in the R Console before rendering:
# install.packages(c("haven", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "knitr", "scales", "DT"))
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
library(DT)

# Read NHANES dataset
demo_data <- read_xpt("DEMO_L.XPT")

# Data preparation
demo_cleaned <- demo_data %>%
  mutate(
    income_4cat = case_when(
      INDFMPIR < 1.30                     ~ "Low Income",
      INDFMPIR >= 1.30 & INDFMPIR < 3.50  ~ "Middle-Low Income",
      INDFMPIR >= 3.50 & INDFMPIR < 5.00  ~ "Middle-High Income",
      INDFMPIR >= 5.00                    ~ "High Income",
      TRUE                                ~ NA_character_
    ) %>% factor(
      levels = c("Low Income", "Middle-Low Income", "Middle-High Income", "High Income")
    ),
    gender = factor(
      ifelse(RIAGENDR == 1, "Male", "Female"),
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_4cat), !is.na(gender))

navy_blue <- "#12263F"
golden_yellow <- "#B88E10"

# Figure 1: Income category bar chart
income_summary <- demo_cleaned %>%
  count(income_4cat) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))

ggplot(income_summary, aes(x = income_4cat, y = proportion, fill = income_4cat)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(n, " (", percent(proportion, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), limits = c(0, max(income_summary$proportion) * 1.15)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Family Income Category Distribution",
    subtitle = "Proportion and total participant counts across income-to-poverty ratio tiers",
    x = "Income Category",
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

# Figure 2: Income category by gender stacked bar chart
ggplot(demo_cleaned, aes(y = income_4cat, fill = gender)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(), name = "Proportion") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(levels(demo_cleaned$income_4cat)), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Male" = navy_blue, "Female" = golden_yellow),
    name = "Gender"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gender Composition Across Income Tiers",
    subtitle = "Percentage breakdown of males and females within each income category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 10),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

# Summary table in the last section
data_table <- demo_cleaned %>%
  group_by(`Income Category` = income_4cat) %>%
  summarise(
    `Total Participants` = n(),
    `Mean Age` = round(mean(RIDAGEYR, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Proportion (%)` = sprintf("%.1f%%", n() / nrow(demo_cleaned) * 100)
  )

kable(
  data_table, 
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Demographic summary metrics by family income categories (NHANES 2021-2023)"
)
```

## Data Appendix

```{r data-table}
# Display the full cleaned dataset as an interactive, searchable table
datatable(
  demo_cleaned,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,      # rows shown per page
    scrollX = TRUE,       # horizontal scroll for wide tables
    autoWidth = TRUE
  ),
  caption = "Full cleaned NHANES 2021-2023 demographic dataset",
  rownames = FALSE
)
```
